'''Collin Yvès Ewald'''  (born 1980 in Basel) is a Swiss scientist investigating the molecular mechanisms of healthy aging.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2018-08-12|title=Dem Alter auf der Spur - Jung bleiben bis ins hohe Alter: Das sagt die Forschung|url=https://www.srf.ch/wissen/gesundheit/dem-alter-auf-der-spur-jung-bleiben-bis-ins-hohe-alter-das-sagt-die-forschung|access-date=2021-11-25|website=Schweizer Radio und Fernsehen (SRF)|language=de}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Gesundes Altern – Fit wie Joe Biden – wie bleibt man im Alter lange gesund?|url=https://www.tagesanzeiger.ch/fit-wie-joe-biden-wie-bleibt-man-im-alter-lange-gesund-704858203320|access-date=2021-11-25|website=Tages-Anzeiger|date=28 November 2020 |language=de}}</ref> He is a [[Molecular Biologist|molecular biologist]] and a professor at [[ETH Zurich]], where he leads the Laboratory of [[Extracellular matrix|Extracellular Matrix]] Regeneration.<ref>{{Cite web|title=23 professors appointed at ETH Zurich and EPFL {{!}} ETH-Board|url=https://www.ethrat.ch/en/medien-medienmitteilungen-news/23-professors-appointed-eth-zurich-and-epfl|access-date=2021-12-02|website=www.ethrat.ch|archive-date=2021-01-15|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210115045039/https://www.ethrat.ch/en/medien-medienmitteilungen-news/23-professors-appointed-eth-zurich-and-epfl}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|last1=Sciences|first1=Address ETH Zürich Dep of Health|last2=Switzerl|first2=Technology Prof Dr Collin Ewald Regenerat Extrazellulärer Matrix SLA C. 8 Schorenstrasse 16 8603 Schwerzenbach|title=Ewald, Collin, Prof. Dr. {{!}} ETH Zurich|url=https://hest.ethz.ch/en/research/professorships/person-detail.MjI0Mjkx.TGlzdC85MiwtNzMwNjY5NDYy.html|access-date=2021-11-25|website=hest.ethz.ch|language=en}}</ref> His [[research]] focuses on the remodeling of the [[extracellular matrix]] during [[Ageing|aging]] and upon [[longevity]] interventions.<ref name=":0">{{Cite ==Career==
Collin Ewald was educated at Mathematisch-Naturwissenschaftliches Gymnasium (MNG) Basel, Switzerland. After completing his bachelor in molecular biology at the [[University of Basel]], he joined the labs of Joy Alcedo and Nancy Hynes studying the function of a breast cancer metastasis gene [[MEMO1|Memo1]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Ewald|first1=Collin Yvès|last2=Hourihan|first2=John M|last3=Bland|first3=Monet S|last4=Obieglo|first4=Carolin|last5=Katic|first5=Iskra|last6=Moronetti Mazzeo|first6=Lorenza E|last7=Alcedo|first7=Joy|last8=Blackwell|first8=T Keith|last9=Hynes|first9=Nancy E|date=2017-01-13|title=NADPH oxidase-mediated redox signaling promotes oxidative stress resistance and longevity through memo-1 in C. elegans|journal=eLife|language=en|volume=6|article-number=e19493|doi=10.7554/eLife.19493|issn=2050-084X|pmc=5235354|pmid=28085666 |doi-access=free }}</ref> in the [[model organism]] ''[[Caenorhabditis elegans|C. elegans]]'' at the [[Friedrich Miescher Institute for Biomedical Research|Friedrich Miescher Institute]] (FMI) for Biomedical Research, Basel, Switzerland. In the Alcedo lab, he became interested in how neurons regulate aging and went on to do a Ph.D. in neuroscience at the [[Graduated Center of the City University of New York]], USA.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Collin Ewald|url=https://www.gc.cuny.edu/About-the-GC/Provost-s-Office/The-Sciences/Spotlight/Contents/Alumni/Biology/Collin-Ewald|access-date=2021-11-25|website=www.gc.cuny.edu|archive-date=2022-01-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220121200617/https://www.gc.cuny.edu/About-the-GC/Provost-s-Office/The-Sciences/Spotlight/Contents/Alumni/Biology/Collin-Ewald|url-status=bot: unknown}}</ref>  Mentored by his Ph.D. supervisor Chris Li, he discovered a conserved genetic link between Insulin/IGF-1 signaling and [[Alzheimer's disease]] [[Amyloid-beta precursor protein|amyloid precursor protein]] (APP) orthologues.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Ewald|first1=Collin Y|last2=Raps|first2=Daniel A|last3=Li|first3=Chris|date=2012-06-01|title=APL-1, the Alzheimer's Amyloid Precursor Protein in Caenorhabditis elegans, Modulates Multiple Metabolic Pathways Throughout Development|journal=Genetics|language=en|volume=191|issue=2|pages=493–507|doi=10.1534/genetics.112.138768|issn=1943-2631|pmc=3374313|pmid=22466039}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|date=2012-06-15|title=Alzheimer's gene 'diabetes link'|language=en-GB|work=BBC News|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/health-18445701|access-date=2021-11-25}}</ref> To deepen his knowledge in aging research, he joined T. Keith Blackwell's lab as a postdoctoral fellow at [[Harvard Medical School]], unraveling the importance of Insulin/IGF-1 signaling in promoting [[collagen]] homeostasis during longevity.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Discovery may hold clues to treatments that slow aging, prevent age-related chronic disease|url=https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2014/12/141215113953.htm|access-date=2021-11-25|website=ScienceDaily|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Center|first=Joslin Diabetes|title=Discovery may hold clues to treatments that slow aging|url=https://medicalxpress.com/news/2014-12-discovery-clues-treatments-aging.html|access-date=2021-11-25|website=medicalxpress.com|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Long Live Collagen|url=https://www.the-scientist.com/the-literature/long-live-collagen-35861|access-date=2021-11-25|website=The Scientist Magazine®|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Grantee in the News: Collin Ewald's Research Explores Collagen and Longevity|url=https://www.afar.org/news/grantee-in-the-news-collin-ewalds-research-explores-collagen-and-longevity|access-date=2021-11-25|website=American Federation for Aging Research|language=en-US}}</ref> In 2015, he became a junior faculty member at the [[Joslin Diabetes Center]], instructor in medicine at Harvard Medical School, and visiting scholar at the [[Whitehead Institute]] ([[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]]). After ten years in the US, in 2016, he secured the [[Swiss National Science Foundation|SNSF]] professorship to return to Switzerland to join the Institute for Translational Medicine.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=People|url=https://itm.ethz.ch/the-institute/people.html|access-date=2021-11-25|website=itm.ethz.ch|language=en}}</ref> as an assistant professor at ETH Zürich.<ref>{{Cite web|title=«Covidisierung» der Forschung verzögert andere Projekte - Echo der Zeit - SRF|url=https://www.srf.ch/audio/echo-der-zeit/covidisierung-der-forschung-verzoegert-andere-projekte?partId=11911214|access-date=2021-11-26|website=Schweizer Radio und Fernsehen (SRF)|language=de}}</ref>

To be at the forefront and to interconnect the two research fields of aging and matrix biology, he founded the Swiss Society for Aging Research,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Swiss Society for Aging Research|url=http://www.ssfar.ch/|access-date=2021-11-26|website=Swiss Society for Aging Research|language=en}}</ref> is the vice president of the German Society of Aging Research,<ref>{{Cite web|title=DGfA e.V. I Deutsche Gesellschaft für Alternsforschung|url=http://alternsforschung.org/|access-date=2021-11-26|website=alternsforschung.org}}</ref> and he re-established the Swiss Society for Matrix Biology.<ref>{{Cite web|title=SSMB|url=http://www.ssmb.ch/|access-date=2021-11-26|website=SSMB|language=en}}</ref> He is an independent scientific advisor of the longevity-start-up-company-builder Maximon AG,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Longevity|url=https://www.maximon.com/|access-date=2021-11-26|website=Maximon|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-04-08|title=#008: Marc Bernegger, Tobias Reichmuth, Collin Ewald (Maximon) - April 8th, 2021|url=https://longevitybiotechshow.com/008-marc-bernegger-tobias-reichmuth-collin-ewald-maximon-april-8-2021/|access-date=2021-11-26|website=Longevity Biotech Show|language=en-US}}</ref> and a co-founder of Avea Life AG.<ref>{{Cite web|title=AVEA|url=https://avea-life.com/password|access-date=2021-11-26|website=AVEA|language=de}}</ref>

== Research ==
His research centers around the remodeling of the [[extracellular matrix]], ensuring tissue and cellular homeostasis during healthy aging.<ref name=":4">{{Citation|title=Collin Ewald presents at ARDD 2021| date=26 October 2021 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dVnH7wKV3G4|language=en|access-date=2021-11-26}}</ref><ref>{{Citation|title=Nano - Play SRF|url=https://www.srf.ch/play/tv/nano/video/nano?urn=urn:srf:video:e2c27d79-b6af-438a-b2ba-f53c9326ab3e|language=de|access-date=2021-11-26}}</ref> In collaboration with Alexandra Naba, he defined the proteins outside of cells forming the extracellular matrix, the so-called matrisome of ''C. elegans''.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Teuscher|first1=Alina C.|last2=Jongsma|first2=Elisabeth|last3=Davis|first3=Martin N.|last4=Statzer|first4=Cyril|last5=Gebauer|first5=Jan M.|last6=Naba|first6=Alexandra|last7=Ewald|first7=Collin Y.|date=February 2019|title=The in-silico characterization of the Caenorhabditis elegans matrisome and proposal of a novel collagen classification|journal=Matrix Biology Plus|language=en|volume=1|article-number=100001|doi=10.1016/j.mbplus.2018.11.001|pmc=7852208|pmid=33543001}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://matrisome.org/|access-date=2021-11-26|website=matrisome.org|title=Matrisome.org}}</ref> Over ten thousand phenotypes stem from mutations in matrisome genes in humans and across species.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Statzer|first1=Cyril|last2=Ewald|first2=Collin Y.|date=November 2020|title=The extracellular matrix phenome across species|journal=Matrix Biology Plus|language=en|volume=8|article-number=100039|doi=10.1016/j.mbplus.2020.100039|pmc=7852310|pmid=33543035}}</ref> He coined the term matreotype<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Ewald|first=Collin Ivès|date=2020|title=The Matrisome during Aging and Longevity: A Systems-Level Approach toward Defining Matreotypes Promoting Healthy Aging|url=https://www.karger.com/Article/FullText/504295|journal=Gerontology|language=en|volume=66|issue=3|pages=266–274|doi=10.1159/000504295|issn=0304-324X|pmc=7214094|pmid=31838471}}</ref><ref name=":5">{{Citation|title=Superhighway of Our Cells: Extracellular Matrix With Prof Collin Ewald| date=9 September 2019 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=j8_6iBP6hqM|language=en|access-date=2021-11-26}}</ref> that is the extracellular matrix composition caused or associated by a cellular or physiological status, genotype, or phenotype. Using gene expression data from humans at different ages and tissues, his team defined the youthful matreotype and used it to predict drugs that slow aging.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Statzer|first1=Cyril|last2=Jongsma|first2=Elisabeth|last3=Liu|first3=Sean X. |last4=Dakhovnik|first4=Alexander|last5=Wandrey|first5=Franziska|last6=Mozharovskyi|first6=Pavlo|last7=Zülli|first7=Fred|last8=Ewald|first8=Collin Y.|date=September 2021|title=Youthful and age-related matreotypes predict drugs promoting longevity|journal=Aging Cell|language=en|volume=20|issue=9|article-number=e13441 |doi=10.1111/acel.13441|doi-access=free |issn=1474-9718|pmc=8441316|pmid=34346557}}</ref> &nbsp;His research group also showed that even close to the end of an individual's life, it is possible to double the lifespan of ''C. elegans''.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Venz|first1=Richard|last2=Pekec|first2=Tina|last3=Katic|first3=Iskra|last4=Ciosk|first4=Rafal|last5=Ewald|first5=Collin Ivès|date=2021-09-10|title=End-of-life targeted degradation of DAF-2 insulin/IGF-1 receptor promotes longevity free from growth-related pathologies|journal=eLife|language=en|volume=10|article-number=e71335|doi=10.7554/eLife.71335|issn=2050-084X|pmc=8492056|pmid=34505574 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

==Distinctions==
He is named under the top 15 Longevity Influencer in Switzerland<ref>{{Cite web|title=Why Switzerland|url=https://www.longevitysuisse.org/why-switzerland|access-date=2021-11-26|website=Longevity Swiss|language=en}}</ref> and world influencer ETH domain,<ref name=":7">{{Cite web|title=ETH / EPFL {{!}} Influencer World Ranking|url=https://ranking.influencer.world/en/set/eth-epfl|access-date=2021-11-25|website=ranking.influencer.world}}</ref> Who is Who in Medical Research,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Who is Who in Medical Research|url=http://www.hochschulmedizin.uzh.ch/en/publications/who-is-who.html|access-date=2021-11-26|website=www.hochschulmedizin.uzh.ch|language=en}}</ref> is in the top 0.5% of the worldwide longevity experts,<ref name=":6">{{Cite web|title=Longevity: Ewald, Collin Y - Expertscape.com|url=https://expertscape.com/au/longevity/Ewald,+Collin+Y|access-date=2021-11-25|website=expertscape.com}}</ref> and has received multiple awards, including the Ellison Medical Foundation and American Federation for Aging Research fellowship in 2013,<ref>{{Cite web|title=2019 Grant Recipients|url=https://www.afar.org/2013-grant-recipients-summaries|access-date=2021-11-26|website=American Federation for Aging Research|language=en-US}}</ref> the [[DeLill Nasser]] Award in 2015,<ref>{{Cite web|title=DeLill Nasser Award for Professional Development in Genetics|url=https://genetics-gsa.org/awards/delill-nasser-award-for-professional-development/|access-date=2021-11-26|website=Genetics Society of America|language=en-US}}</ref> and the SNSF Professorship in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web|title=SNSF {{!}} P3 Research Database {{!}} Project 163898|url=http://p3.snf.ch/|access-date=2021-11-26|website=p3.snf.ch|language=en}}</ref>
